title: Growth-Arc sync prep: Marcus check-in + next-cycle signals
content:
Purpose / context:
- Quick sync to calibrate Marcus's growth arc (IC -> Staff trajectory), unblock any execution blockers for Sprint 34, and align on stretch project options for Q4.
- Marcus recently rotated off the latency budget task; want to check signal-to-noise on his bandwidth and motivation for an owner-level scope.

Top objectives for this 1:1 (30 min):
1) Well-being check & energy: are deadlines draining or energizing? (5 min)
2) Career coaching: assess interest in taking a lead on the model-variant routing experiment (15 min)
3) Tactical unblock: identify blockers re: infra quotas and dedupe tasks with platform team (7 min)
4) Action and follow-ups: capture next steps and owners (3 min)

Pre-read I sent Marcus: short note listing three possible lead scopes (variant routing, KV-cache telemetry, higher-quantization evals). He replied "leaning towards routing but worried about execution bandwidth".

Notes to self before conversation:
- Marcus's recent PRs: 3 small fixes + one large refactor (see PRs in linked_artifacts). He has been shipping but still defers some decisions to senior ICs.
- Performance profile: strong technical depth, needs practice in cross-team influence and written proposals.
- Motivation clues: referenced wanting "larger impact work," but also asked for fewer on-call nights last month. Might be at risk of overload.

Suggested framing language (use in meeting):
- "I want to understand what kinds of impact feel energizing to you and where you want to grow this quarter."
- "If you picked the routing experiment, what would success look like in 6 weeks? How would we measure it?"
- "If you take the lead, what parts would you want from platform / infra to be owned by them vs you?"

Questions to ask Marcus (quick checklist):
- 1) On a scale 1-10, how’s your current energy for taking a multi-sprint project?
- 2) What are the top 2 technical risks you foresee with model-variant routing?
- 3) Which stakeholders would we need buy-in from, and have you had any conversations with them already?
- 4) Are there routine tasks I can remove or reassign to free up ~8 hours/week?
- 5) Anything I should surface to your IC peers to help unblock cross-team work?

Potential pitfalls & scripts:
- If Marcus says he’s overloaded: propose a 6-week pilot with a clear stopping criterion and a co-owner from platform (script: "Let's design a 6-week experiment with weekly checkpoints and a safety valve if it blocks shipping work").
- If Marcus is enthusiastic but unsure about cross-team influence: offer to set up a kickoff with leads and to draft the initial problem statement together.
- If he declines: test the small-ownership option (e.g., own metrics and rollout plan, not the infra implementation).

Concrete success metrics to propose for routing experiment (for alignment):
- Metric 1: 95th p95 latency regression ≤ 3% vs baseline for the first 10k requests in canary.
- Metric 2: Cost-per-response lower by ≥ 8% in controlled traffic split after autoscaling rules applied.
- Metric 3: Clear rollback plan and automated fallback implemented and tested in staging.

Immediate action items (capture during meeting):
- A1: If Marcus picks lead, owner: Marcus; deliverable: 1-page experiment brief + measurement plan; due: 2026-08-21.
- A2: Identify platform co-owner for infra tasks, owner: Brynn to propose; due: 2026-08-12 (intro + ask for 2-3 hours/week of support).
- A3: Reassign two recurring non-critical tasks (code reviews on repo X) to Chloe for next 3 sprints; owner: Brynn; due: 2026-08-15.
- A4: Schedule a 30-min kickoff with product lead (Ava) + infra lead (Samir); owner: Brynn; due: 2026-08-14.
- A5: Marcus to draft initial success metrics and a single slide of rollout plan; owner: Marcus; due: 2026-08-18.

Post-meeting follow-ups I will do (notes to self):
- Send a short recap email with decisions and owners within 24 hours.
- Create INF ticket for the routing experiment with clear acceptance criteria and link to Marcus's slide.
- Block 1 hour on Marcus's calendar next week for proposal workshop (invite: Brynn, Marcus, Ava).

Open questions / things to probe if time allows:
- Is Marcus leaning toward individual contributor growth (deep technical craft) vs. people leadership in the longer term?
- How does he feel about writing short proposals for stakeholders (comfort and bandwidth)?
- Any friction from recent handoff with the latency budget team that I should surface to SRE?

Tone reminders to myself:
- Keep it coach-like: ask open questions, avoid prescribing too much unless he requests support.
- Use concrete offers: introductions, help drafting the one-pager, blocking time.
- Surface trade-offs explicitly (impact vs. bandwidth vs. career signal).

Quick retro from last 1:1 (3 bullets):
- Marcus shipped the refactor on schedule and reduced CI flakiness by ~12% (call this out).
- He asked for clearer prioritization—I've not tightened our sprint commitments enough.
- He appreciated the 1:1 buffer time last week for career chat.

End-of-meeting checklist (to complete in 2 min):
- Confirm top 1-2 decisions verbally.
- Read back action items + owners + due dates.
- Agree a date/time for the next check: tentative 2026-08-22.

Scratch ideas (if Marcus wants stretch but not full ownership):
- Option A: Marcus owns experiment metrics and rollout playbook; platform owns infra implementation.
- Option B: Marcus leads a two-sprint spike to validate feasibility and collects telemetry samples; no production rollout commitment.
- Option C: Pair Marcus with a senior IC for mentorship and stakeholder introductions for the first 6 weeks.

Random notes to file (for future reference):
- Marcus mentioned interest in conference speaking; link to "talk prep" resource page after meeting.
- Track his on-call nights next quarter to avoid stacking with project ramp.

— end of prep —

(If this goes well: formalize the 6-week experiment in Confluence and loop in product for KPI sign-off.)
